newsitem.title: FRANCE: BP France to run Mobil stations.
newsitem.headline: BP France to run Mobil stations.

text.p: BP France, a subsidiary of the British Petrolem Co, said it would run the French service stations of Mobil Corporation from January 1 following a European joint venture deal of the parent groups.
In a statement, BP France said it would have a 70 percent stake in a new company while Mobil Oil Francaise would have 30 percent.
The new company will operate all car fuel, house fuel and LPG operations and in particular a network of 800 service stations in France. Mobil stations will gradually be transformed into BP livery.
Mobil will run the oils and special products activities through another joint venture in which Mobil has 51 percent and BP France 49 percent.
This involves products from the refineries of Notre-Dame-de-Gravenchon and Dunkirk.
The BP and Mobil brands will be maintained.
Chemical activities, as well as aviation and shipping fuels and shipping activities are not affected by the restructuring.
The companies gave no financial details.
The original joint venture deal was announced in February and obtained European Union approval in August.

On Friday, BP and Mobil said the joint venture would exceed their original estimates and annual benefits would be more than the forecast figure of between $400 million and $500 million pre-tax in annual cost savings.
